segments.say: You step through the little gate into a quiet garden at night. The air is cool and soft, and smells of damp earth and leaves. Above you, the sky is full of stars now. Everything here is still, as if the whole garden is resting, and has been waiting for you to rest too.

The ground beneath your feet is soft, a mossy path between low plants. Each step sinks in gently and makes almost no sound. You walk slowly, more slowly than before, letting your eyes adjust to the gentle darkness.

Little by little, the garden shows itself to you. Pale flowers that only open in the evening, glowing faintly in the dark. Leaves glistening with the first drops of dew. A small pond, perfectly still, holding the reflection of the stars. And all around, the soft, steady song of crickets.

show.title: In the garden
items: Pale flowers open in the dark
A small pond holding the stars

segments.say: Nothing in this garden is in a hurry. The plants grow in their own time. The flowers open when they're ready. No one tells them how fast to grow or when to bloom. They are free to be exactly what they are.

show.cap: A garden resting under the stars

segments.say: Maybe that's how rest works too. You can't force it. You can't make yourself fall asleep, any more than you can make a flower open. You can only make a quiet space, and let it come in its own time. And that's what you're doing now.

Wander over to the edge of the little pond. Kneel down, or sit on the cool grass beside it. Look at the water. It's so still that the stars seem to float inside it. Not a ripple. Not a sound. Just calm, clear stillness.

Let your mind become like that water. If a thought comes, like a small ripple, just watch it spread out and fade. There's no need to chase it, and no need to stop it. Give it a moment, and the surface becomes smooth again, quiet and clear.

Breathe with the garden for a while. Breathe in the cool night air. Breathe out what's left of the day. Breathe in the stillness of the pond. And breathe out everything else, everything you no longer need to carry tonight.

A soft breeze moves through the garden. It touches the leaves, and they whisper. It brushes your face, cool and kind. Then it passes, and everything is still again. Let your body feel as light and easy as that breeze.

Nearby, there's a patch of soft grass, open to the sky. If you like, lie back on it. Feel the earth beneath you, steady and patient, holding your whole weight. Look up at the stars, or let your eyes close. Either is fine.

The ground holds you completely. Your head, your shoulders, your back, your arms, your legs. There's nothing you need to hold up, and nothing you need to hold on to. You can let go of all of it, and still be perfectly held.

All around you, the garden goes on resting. The stars turning slowly overhead. The crickets singing their soft, steady song. The pale flowers resting in the dark. And inside you, a warm, quiet sense of peace.

You may feel yourself drifting deeper now. Your body heavier. Your breathing softer. Your thoughts slower, further apart, like stars with wide, dark spaces between them. Let yourself sink into those quiet spaces.

In this garden, there's no schedule. The moon rises when it rises. The dew gathers when it gathers. Even the crickets will fall quiet whenever they're ready, and not a moment before. Let yourself belong to that slow, unhurried time, where nothing has to happen next.

show.cap: The garden keeps its own time

segments.say: You're free to stay here as long as you like. Free to listen, or to stop listening. Free to drift off whenever sleep arrives. The garden will be here, quiet and patient, keeping watch over you through the night.
